<reason>B wins the comparative policy argument. A establishes a credible fairness problem, but does not adequately justify annual whole-fortune taxation over targeting untaxed gains. B distinguishes feasible valuation from equitable annual enforcement, answers the double-taxation question directly, and exposes A's unequal political-feasibility standard. A's later defenses depend on unsupported claims about immobile wealth and annually revisited exemptions, while conflating genuine investment losses with concealed appreciation. B consistently narrows and resolves these clashes; A's closing largely repeats arguments already damaged.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's strongest rebuttal is that annual assessment does not make statutory exemptions expire or opaque ownership transparent. This directly defeats A's claim that recurrence makes wealth taxation harder to sabotage, leaving A without its principal reason to distrust targeted reform while trusting wealth-tax design.</best_rebuttal>
